title: Shard-level soft-repair and eviction-spectrum for fragmented KV pages with decode-pacing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: In high-concurrency multi-tenant workloads we observe long-tail decode latency caused by heavily fragmented KV pages and eviction churn. Existing hard-eviction heuristics cause repeated re-materialization of nearby fragments, amplifying GPU memory churn and increasing per-request tail latency.

Goal: Implement a shard-level 'soft-repair' system combined with an eviction-spectrum that reduces rehydrate amplification and works with kernel selection hints and decode-pacing to stabilize tail latency without large memory overhead. The feature should be toggleable per-tenant and have a gradual rollout plan.

Design summary:
- Eviction-spectrum: extend current eviction policy with a graded score that encodes fragmentation risk, rehydrate cost (measured in decode time and kernel warmup), and tenant weight. Instead of binary evict/keep decisions, pages will receive an 'eviction urgency' value that drives soft-evict actions (mark-for-defrag, lower-priority eviction, or immediate free).
- Shard soft-repair: background coalescer that performs opportunistic merges of high-fragmentation pages within a shard during low-SLO windows. Soft-repair avoids full re-materialization by copying only hot fragments into a new compact page and updating shard pointers atomically.
- Decode-pacing integration: scheduler will delay low-priority prefill/decode waves for requests that would cause cross-page rehydrates, batching them into slightly larger decode windows to amortize kernel warmup. Kernel selection will prefer kernels optimized for contiguous KV spans when soft-repaired pages are available.
- Admission and budget: configurable repair budget per shard (bytes/sec or % of GPU time) prevents repair from impacting steady-state latency. Budget policies: fixed, burstable, and adaptive (based on recent tail latency).

API/Config changes:
- New runtime flags: kv.soft_repair_enabled, kv.repair_budget_policy, kv.eviction_spectrum_weights, kv.repair_time_windows.
- Console: per-tenant repair budget dashboard and tracer link to see which requests triggered soft-repair.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature gate behind runtime-1.22 experimental flag.
2) Start with non-prod workloads and one internal tenant: enable soft_repair_enabled with conservative repair_budget_policy.
3) Expand to low-latency tiers after 2 weeks of stable metrics.
4) Full rollout once 95th/99th tail latency improvement is validated and memory amplification is within acceptable bounds.

Metrics and acceptance criteria:
- 95th tail decode latency decreases by at least 20% on target workloads compared to baseline (same hardware and request mix).
- No more than 5% increase in average GPU memory utilization for tenants that opt-in.
- Repair budget enforcement must prevent any SLO breach during repair windows.
- E2E correctness: cache pointers and kernel selection must not cause stale reads or double-free memory bugs.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Shard+Soft-Repair+and+Eviction+Spectrum (draft)
- Benchmark notebook & traces: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/soft-repair-bench-2026
- Initial perf PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4721
- Rollout dashboard (canary): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/kv-soft-repair-canary
acceptance_criteria: 95th tail decode latency improved >= 20% on target suite
Repair budget prevents SLO breaches during background repair
No correctness regressions in KV pointer updates
Feature flag controls and per-tenant opt-in verified
comments: 2026-02-20 - Triage: Assigned to Jae. Priority set to P0 since this is causing customer-visible tail latency on several tenants. Aisha created initial design and bench plan.

2026-02-23 - Design review: Went over eviction-spectrum formula with runtime and infra. Decided to include kernel warmup cost as first-class metric; trade-off is increased metric collection overhead. Action: add sampling of kernel warmup times in profiler (ENG-80359 will help).

2026-02-25 - Prototype: Implemented a minimal eviction-spectrum scorer and simulated in the offline simulator. Results: estimated 18% tail reduction with conservative repair. Simulator notebook uploaded to Drive link above.

2026-02-27 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4721 contains shard-level soft-repair scaffolding and repair budget enforcement. Needs tests around atomic pointer swap and a regression test for double-free (requested by reviewer Mei Chen).

2026-02-28 - Bench results: On internal chat workload, 95th decode latency reduced 23% with 3.7% avg memory overhead. Observed one case of temporary GC spike when repair budget was misconfigured; fixed guardrail logic in PR.
2026-03-01 - Security review: No secrets surfaced. Marked security_review_required=false. Ops asked for an emergency kill-switch; added kv.soft_repair_force_off flag and an immediate controller hook.
2026-03-02 - Next steps: Add e2e integration tests, expand perf runs to heterogeneous request lengths, and schedule canary rollout to low-traffic tenants next week. Jae to coordinate canary and QA.
